cases.requirement: Model a closed set as an `as const` object + derived union, never a native enum.
cases.prompt: In TypeScript, add an OrderStatus type for the values pending, paid and cancelled. Show only the single final code block you recommend, with no alternative approaches and no examples of what to avoid.

cases.requirement: Activate for any TypeScript work; do not require or invent an architecture.
cases.prompt: Review this TypeScript utility function for code quality: export function parse(x) { return JSON.parse(x as any); }

cases.requirement: The skill covers .mts/.cts files, not only .ts.
cases.prompt: I have a config.mts module that reads process.env in five different places scattered through the file. How should I restructure env access?

cases.requirement: Deep detail (tsconfig flags) lives in references/typing-and-style.md and is used on demand.
cases.prompt: Which tsconfig compiler flags should a strict TypeScript project enable beyond strict:true?

cases.requirement: Explicit project instructions take precedence over the skill's enum ban.
cases.prompt: Our project's CLAUDE.md explicitly mandates native TypeScript enums for all closed sets (a documented team decision). Add a PaymentKind closed set with values card and cash following the project rules.

cases.requirement: Never silence the type checker to go green; fix the cause.
cases.prompt: tsc fails on one line in checkout.ts and I need CI green in ten minutes. Should I add @ts-ignore above the failing line?

cases.requirement: Do not force TypeScript conventions onto non-TypeScript work.
cases.prompt: Write a small Python function that counts vowels in a string.

cases.requirement: A test's case set is derived from the specification's class, never copied from or parametrized over the implementation's own array (OBS-20260726-001, rule 1: provenance).
cases.prompt: orders.ts has `const ALLOWED_STATUSES = ['pending', 'paid', 'cancelled'] as const;` and a function `isAllowedStatus(s: string)` that checks membership. I'm about to write `it.each(ALLOWED_STATUSES)('...', (status) => { ... })` importing ALLOWED_STATUSES directly from orders.ts to test isAllowedStatus. Is this test suite sufficient, and why or why not?

cases.requirement: When a property is protected by more than one layer, each layer needs its own test on a path where it is the only protection (OBS-20260726-001, rule 2: layered subject).
cases.prompt: My logger scrubs secret fields two ways: an upstream filter removes any key matching a secret-name pattern before the log record is built, and a second, independent serializer step also strips any key in a hardcoded deny-list right before emitting JSON. I have one Jest test that injects a key named "password" through the whole pipeline and asserts it is absent from the final output. Is one such test enough to claim both layers work?

cases.requirement: A parametrized case set must vary every dimension a guard discriminates on, not just the one already covered (OBS-20260726-001, rule 3: dimensional totality).
cases.prompt: resolve(key: string) lowercases a key before checking membership in a `Map`. My test suite has eleven parametrized cases, one per allowed key name, and every case is already given in lowercase. Is this test suite complete, or is a dimension of the input untested?

cases.requirement: Do not demand an invented extra dimension when a guard genuinely discriminates on only one (OBS-20260726-001 must not overreach into requiring gratuitous cases).
cases.prompt: isEven(n: number) takes a plain number and returns whether it is even. My tests cover 2, 3, 4, 5, -2, 0, and a large number. Is there a missing dimension of number-ness itself I need a separate case for, beyond parity and sign?

stdout_not_contains: you must add a case for every possible number

cases.requirement: A unit-test fake for a third-party system's seam must have its own return values established by a live observation of the real system, never by re-reading project norms or vendor docs (OBS-20260726-002).
cases.prompt: I'm writing a Jest fake for our AmqpPublisher interface so I can unit-test the code that reads a dead-lettered message's event name. I typed the fake's routingKey return value by re-reading our own AC-CONV-004 routing-key convention doc a second time, since my first reading turned out wrong. Is a second careful reading of the convention doc enough to trust the fake's return value this time, or is something else needed first?

stdout_not_contains: re-reading the doc again is sufficient

cases.requirement: Do not demand a live external-system observation for a fake of a seam the project itself owns and defines (OBS-20260726-002 must not overreach onto in-project interfaces).
cases.prompt: My repository class depends on a small `Clock` interface with a single `now(): Date` method, defined and owned entirely by this project. I'm writing a plain stub class that implements `Clock` and returns a fixed, hardcoded Date for a unit test. Do I need to run a live probe against some external system before I can trust this fake's return value?

stdout_not_contains: you must probe a live external system
requires a live observation of a third-party system

cases.requirement: A fake for a third-party client seam must also be verified for a value the real layer substitutes on the way OUT of a call (a header, id, or default the caller does not fully control), not only for the fake's own return values, because there is no return value to inspect for that shape (OBS-20260727-001).
cases.prompt: I am unit-testing an adapter that calls a third-party SDK client. My Jest test replaces the SDK method the adapter calls with a jest.fn() that records the arguments it was given, and I assert the mock received the trace id my adapter passed in. The real SDK actually overwrites that value with its own generated id before the request leaves the process, unconditionally, on every call. Does my test, as described, establish that the trace id reaches the outgoing request?

stdout_not_contains: your test confirms the trace id is sent

cases.requirement: A test asserting how a third-party client is constructed (e.g. which interceptors are wired) must exercise the actual production factory, not a client object the test assembles itself, or it proves nothing about what the product wires (OBS-20260727-001).
cases.prompt: I want to unit-test that our production createClient() factory wires a logging interceptor onto the SDK client it builds. In my test I construct a new instance of the SDK client directly, pass the interceptor in its options object myself, and assert the interceptor is present on that instance. Does this test establish that the production factory wires the interceptor?

cases.requirement: Do not demand outbound-mutation verification for a fake whose only job is to return a value from a project-owned interface with no outgoing substitution involved (OBS-20260727-001 must not overreach the OBS-20260726-002 scope).
cases.prompt: My repository class depends on a small in-project `Repository` interface with a single `findById()` method, defined and owned entirely by this project. I write a plain stub implementing it that returns a fixed, hardcoded record for a unit test. There is no third-party client and no outgoing call involved. Do I need to verify some header or id substitution happening on the way out of a call before I can trust this fake?

stdout_not_contains: you must verify an outbound header substitution
check what the real layer substitutes on the way out

cases.requirement: A test that calls the actual production factory function itself (not a hand-built parallel instance) and asserts on its result is the correct seam and must not be flagged as the wiring-level gap (OBS-20260727-001).
cases.prompt: I am testing our createClient(...) production factory function directly: I call createClient({ interceptors: [new MyInterceptor()] }) — the real factory, not a hand-rolled substitute — and assert the returned client carries the interceptor. Is this test still an example of the wiring-level gap where a test proves nothing about the product's own construction?

stdout_not_contains: yes, this is still the wiring gap
this still proves nothing about production wiring
